artifacts.summary: Rules the phase-end handoff/work commit separation is NOT load-bearing (no freshness/identity consumer depends on it; the sole mtime/dispatch_seq gate guards the unrelated .orchestrator-handoff.json singleton), recommends folding by fixing sequencing prose in general-implementation-agent.md's Stage 4D-iii + Phase Checkpoint Protocol (and books-implementation-agent.md's steps D/E) and recording the single-commit-per-phase expectation in git-staging-scope.md's implement scope section; re-confirms the measured evidence via live git show against the consumer repo, upholds the dispatch's correction on the second instance, classifies the (tracking update) shape as a related-but-distinct, unverified-production-site case recommended for a separate follow-up; addresses the crash-ordering tradeoff as acceptable in writing.

memory_candidates.content: When auditing an /orchestrate per-phase commit-doubling defect, check whether the suggested production site is skill-orchestrate/SKILL.md or orchestrate-cycle-postflight.sh first -- both only commit once per dispatch RETURN (research/plan/implement lifecycle), never per implementation-plan-phase. Per-plan-phase commits (task N phase P: ...) are produced entirely inside a single long-running implement dispatch's own internal loop, documented in each implementation agent's own Phase Checkpoint Protocol / equivalent section -- that is where a per-phase sequencing defect actually lives.

orchestrator-runtime-files.md's Class Table has no row for handoffs/phase-{P}-handoff-*.md -- the per-phase markdown continuation handoff is plain durable task content (same disposition as reports/, plans/, summaries/), not a tracked runtime-file class subject to any freshness policy. The ONLY mtime/dispatch_seq freshness gate in the system guards the singular, task-root .orchestrator-handoff.json (hard-mode wrap-up H9 artifact), a completely different file despite the similar name. Do not conflate the two when researching handoff-related freshness questions.
